overview: Narrative review of heat-health plan activation and emergency care, lowering thresholds, equity and activation costs, written for a non-clinical board, with the certainty of each finding stated.
population: Studies and reports on residents exposed to heat in temperate regions, with attention to older people living alone and low-income neighbourhoods.
exposure: Heat-health plan activation, its components (alerts, cooling centres, outreach, hospital preparation) and changes to activation thresholds.
procedures: Searches of three bibliographic databases and public health agency websites for 2010 onward; one reviewer screens and a second checks a sample; structured extraction of design, setting, outcome and equity results; certainty described in words for each finding; costs described alongside effects without combining them.

outcomes.name: Heat-related emergency department visits and ambulance calls
outcomes.measure: Direction and size of change associated with activation, as reported

outcomes.name: Effect of lowering the threshold
outcomes.measure: Change in activation days and in heat-related visits, as reported

outcomes.name: Effects by age, living alone and neighbourhood income
Costs and alert fatigue
outcomes.measure: Reported activation costs and reports of alert fatigue
outcomes.why: What more activation days would cost.

outcomes.name: Search coverage
outcomes.measure: Sources searched and grey reports included
outcomes.why: Shows what the review could and could not find.

feasibility: Two people over the winter; deliverable by April 2027.

biasFlags.label: Selective inclusion
biasFlags.note: Narrative reviews can favour convenient studies; inclusion rules written in advance.

parsimony.simplestPath: One primary synthesis target, two secondary, costs alongside.

summary: Narrative review protocol with standard outcome roles.
